sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: This is a collection of simple PyTorch implementations of well-known deep learning papers, from transformers and LoRA to diffusion models and GANs. Each one is heavily commented, and the nn.labml.ai website shows the code and explanations side by side.
sixtySeconds.problem: Research papers are dense and official code is often hard to follow. These short, annotated implementations let you read an algorithm line by line next to a plain explanation.
whoFor: Engineers who want to understand a paper's core idea
Researchers looking for clean reference code
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for readable, annotated reference code covering dozens of papers, actively maintained with new implementations added often.

overview: Topics include transformers (multi-head attention, rotary embeddings, ALiBi, Transformer XL, ViT and many variants), LoRA, GPT-NeoX, diffusion models (DDPM, DDIM, latent diffusion, Stable Diffusion), GANs (DCGAN, CycleGAN, WGAN, StyleGAN 2), LSTMs, ResNet and more.
The easiest way to read them is the website nn.labml.ai, which renders each file as side-by-side notes. To run or reuse the code, install the labml-nn package with pip.
The README also points to an Annotated Implementation Skill that coding agents can use to implement any paper with annotations in the same style.
